cashTip: Norway is almost cashless; cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for tiny amounts.
name: Oslo
tagline: Fjord-side museums and bold new architecture
summary: Norway's capital sits at the head of the Oslofjord, with forests and ski slopes on its edge. You can walk on the roof of the marble Opera House, see Munch's The Scream, explore polar ships and Viking history, and swim or sauna in the harbour.
seasonNote: May to September has long light days; June and July nights barely get dark. Winter is cold and snowy, with skiing at Holmenkollen. Norway is expensive all year.
arrival: Oslo Airport Gardermoen is 20 minutes from the centre on the Flytoget express train. Trains run from Stockholm (about 5 hours) and Bergen (7 hours).
gettingAround: Metro, trams, buses and harbour ferries share Ruter tickets; the centre is walkable.
foodTip: Open sandwiches, fish soup, brown cheese (brunost) and cinnamon buns.
buyTip: Norwegian wool sweaters, brunost, design homeware and aquavit.

connections.note: Overnight DFDS ferry, or a 70-minute flight.

items.name: Oslo Opera House
items.summary: A white marble opera house you can walk up onto, sloping into the fjord.
items.expect: The roof is free and open all day.

items.name: Munch Museum
items.summary: A tall new museum holding Edvard Munch's work, including versions of The Scream.
items.expect: The Scream versions are shown in rotation.
items.tip: Ride to the top floor for fjord views.

items.name: Vigeland Sculpture Park
items.summary: Over 200 sculptures of the human figure by Gustav Vigeland in Frogner Park.
items.tip: See the Monolith of tangled bodies.
items.why: The world's largest sculpture park by one artist.

items.name: Fram Museum
items.summary: The polar ship Fram, used by Nansen and Amundsen, which you can climb aboard.
items.expect: Next to the Kon-Tiki Museum on Bygdøy.
items.tip: Take the summer ferry from the City Hall pier.

items.name: Norwegian Folk Museum
items.summary: An open-air museum of old farmhouses and a medieval stave church.

items.name: Akershus Fortress
items.summary: A medieval castle and fortress on the harbour with free grounds.
items.expect: The grounds are free; the castle has a fee.
items.tip: Walk the walls for harbour views.

items.name: Holmenkollen ski jump
items.summary: A famous ski jump with a ski museum and a zipline.
items.tip: Go up the jump tower for the view.

items.name: Mathallen food hall
items.summary: An indoor food hall with Norwegian cheeses, seafood and cafés.

items.name: Open sandwiches
items.summary: Rye bread piled with shrimp, salmon or egg.

items.name: Brown cheese and waffles
items.summary: Sweet caramel-like brown cheese on waffles or bread.
items.tip: Try it on a heart-shaped waffle.

cashTip: Norway is almost cashless; cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for tiny amounts.
name: Bergen
summary: Bergen is a harbour city between seven mountains, with the colourful wooden warehouses of Bryggen on its waterfront. A funicular climbs Mount Fløyen, the fish market sells the morning catch, and it's the starting point for the great western fjords.
seasonNote: May to September is best. It's one of Europe's rainiest cities, so bring a raincoat in any season.
arrival: Bergen Airport is 20 minutes from the centre by light rail. The Bergen Line train from Oslo takes about 7 hours; Hurtigruten coastal ships start here.
gettingAround: The centre is walkable; the light rail and buses go further.
foodTip: Bergen fish soup, fresh shrimp and skillingsboller cinnamon buns.
buyTip: Wool knitwear, trolls and local art.

connections.note: The Bergen Line, one of the world's great train rides.

items.name: Bryggen
items.summary: A row of wooden Hanseatic warehouses, with crooked passages behind.
items.tip: Walk the narrow alleys behind the façades.

items.name: Mount Fløyen
items.summary: A funicular to a viewpoint over the city, with forest trails at the top.
items.expect: Queues in summer; walking down is easy.
items.tip: Take the funicular up and walk down.

items.name: Mount Ulriken
items.summary: The highest of Bergen's seven mountains, with a cable car.
items.expect: A ridge hike connects it to Fløyen.
items.tip: Hike Ulriken to Fløyen on a clear day.
items.why: Big views over fjords and islands.

items.name: KODE art museums
items.summary: Four art museums by a lake, with Munch and Norwegian painters.

items.name: Troldhaugen
items.summary: Composer Edvard Grieg's villa and concert hall by a lake.

items.name: Fjord cruise
items.summary: A boat trip into the narrow Mostraumen strait and Osterfjord.

items.name: Flåm and Nærøyfjord
items.summary: The steep Flåm railway and a cruise on the narrow Nærøyfjord.
items.expect: A long day trip, often as 'Norway in a Nutshell'.
items.tip: Book seats on the left side of the Flåm train going down.

items.name: Fish market
items.summary: Stalls selling shrimp, salmon, king crab and fish soup by the harbour.
items.tip: Have a shrimp baguette by the water.

items.name: Bergen fish soup
items.summary: A creamy fish soup with vegetables.

items.name: Skillingsbolle
items.summary: Big cinnamon buns from Bergen's bakeries.

cashTip: Norway is almost cashless; cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for tiny amounts.
name: Tromsø
tagline: Northern lights and the midnight sun
summary: Tromsø sits 350 km north of the Arctic Circle, ringed by snowy peaks and fjords. From September to March it's one of the best places on earth to see the northern lights, and from May to July the sun never sets.
seasonNote: Northern lights season runs from September to March, on clear dark nights. Polar night (late November to mid-January) has no sunrise. The midnight sun lasts from late May to late July.
arrival: Fly from Oslo (about 2 hours). The airport is 10 minutes from the centre. Hurtigruten coastal ships also stop here.
gettingAround: Walkable centre; buses and tour pick-ups for trips out of town.
foodTip: Arctic char, reindeer stew (bidos), king crab and a Mack beer.
buyTip: Sami crafts, wool and Arctic-themed design.

connections.note: Or a scenic drive of about 7 hours.

items.name: Northern lights chase
items.summary: Guided trips drive away from city lights and clouds to find the aurora.
items.expect: Night tours from September to March; no sighting is guaranteed.
items.tip: Book a small-group chase with photos included.

items.name: Arctic Cathedral
items.summary: A white church shaped like ice floes, with a huge glass mosaic.
items.tip: Visit at dusk or for a concert.

items.name: Fjellheisen cable car
items.summary: A cable car to a viewpoint 421 m above the city.
items.expect: Great for aurora on clear nights.
items.tip: Go at sunset, or after dark for the lights.

items.name: Polaria
items.summary: An Arctic aquarium shaped like toppled ice blocks, with bearded seals.
items.expect: Seal feeding several times a day.

items.name: Polar Museum
items.summary: A museum of Arctic hunting and the great polar expeditions.

items.name: Dog sledding
items.summary: Drive your own team of huskies across the snow.

items.name: Sommarøy
items.summary: A fishing village with white beaches and turquoise water.
items.tip: Drive the scenic route over Kvaløya.

items.name: Arctic char
items.summary: A local cold-water fish, often smoked or pan-fried.
items.tip: Try it smoked as a starter.

items.name: Reindeer stew (bidos)
items.summary: A Sami stew of reindeer, potatoes and carrots.
items.expect: Served at Sami camps and restaurants.
items.tip: Try it at a Sami camp.

items.name: Mack beer hall
items.summary: One of the world's most northerly breweries and its old beer hall.

cashTip: Norway is almost cashless; cards and phone payments work everywhere, even for tiny amounts.
name: Lofoten Islands
summary: The Lofoten Islands rise from the sea in a wall of jagged peaks, with red fishermen's cabins (rorbuer) on stilts, white beaches and drying racks of cod. Summer brings the midnight sun and hiking; winter brings northern lights over the fjords.
seasonNote: June to August has the midnight sun and the best hiking. February to March brings the skrei cod season and good northern lights. Weather changes fast at any time of year.
arrival: Fly from Bodø to Leknes or Svolvær, or take the car ferry from Bodø to Moskenes (about 3 to 4 hours). Hurtigruten ships stop at Svolvær and Stamsund.
gettingAround: Rent a car; a single road (the E10) runs the length of the islands.
foodTip: Stockfish, fresh cod (skrei) in winter, fish cakes and fish soup.
baseArea: A rorbu cabin in Reine, Hamnøy or Henningsvær

connections.note: Via Bodø; or a scenic drive.

items.name: Reine
items.summary: A fishing village of red cabins below sheer peaks, often called Norway's most beautiful.
items.expect: The view from the bridge is the classic photo.

items.name: Reinebringen hike
items.summary: A steep stone-stair climb to a view over Reine and the fjords.
items.expect: About 2 to 3 hours return; very steep.

items.name: Hamnøy
items.summary: A cluster of red rorbuer on rocks, the most photographed spot in Lofoten.

items.name: Henningsvær
items.summary: A fishing village on small islands, with a famous football pitch on the rocks.
items.tip: See the football pitch from above.

items.name: Lofotr Viking Museum
items.summary: A reconstructed Viking chieftain's longhouse on the original site.
items.expect: Summer has Viking activities and a feast.

items.name: Nusfjord
items.summary: One of Norway's oldest and best-preserved fishing villages.
items.tip: Visit the old cod liver oil factory.
items.why: Fishing history in a tiny harbour.

items.name: Å
items.summary: The village at the end of the road, with a stockfish museum.
items.expect: At the very end of the E10.

items.name: Stockfish
items.summary: Cod air-dried on wooden racks for months, eaten in stews or as snacks.

items.name: Fresh cod (skrei)
items.summary: Winter cod, poached with liver and roe in the traditional way.

items.name: Fish cakes
items.summary: Soft fish cakes from local cod, sold at fish shops.
items.tip: Buy them warm from a fish shop.

cashTip: Carry pesos in small notes for jeepneys, tricycles and small shops; ATMs can run dry on islands, so bring enough cash.
name: Manila
tagline: A Spanish walled city in a buzzing metropolis
summary: The Philippine capital is a vast, chaotic metropolis around the old Spanish walled city of Intramuros, with stone churches, forts and colonial houses. Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown, and the sunsets over Manila Bay are highlights.
seasonNote: December to April is dry; March to May is hottest. June to November is the rainy season with typhoons.
arrival: Ninoy Aquino International Airport is 30 to 90 minutes from the centre depending on traffic; use Grab or airport taxis.
gettingAround: Traffic is heavy; use Grab, the LRT trains and walk within Intramuros.
foodTip: Adobo, sinigang, lechon, halo-halo and Chinese food in Binondo.
buyTip: Dried mangoes, barong shirts and woven goods.

connections.note: Small planes to El Nido or flights to Puerto Princesa.

items.name: Intramuros
items.summary: The 16th-century Spanish walled city of churches, plazas and stone houses.
items.expect: Walk or rent a bamboo bike.

items.name: San Agustin Church
items.summary: The oldest stone church in the Philippines, with trompe-l'oeil ceilings.

items.name: Fort Santiago
items.summary: A Spanish fort where national hero José Rizal was held before his execution.
items.tip: Follow Rizal's footsteps marked in brass.

items.name: National Museum of Fine Arts
items.summary: Free national galleries, including Juan Luna's giant Spoliarium.

items.name: Rizal Park
items.summary: A large park with the Rizal Monument.
items.expect: Changing of the guard at the monument.
items.tip: Walk on to Manila Bay for sunset.

items.name: Binondo
items.summary: The world's oldest Chinatown, founded in 1594.

items.name: Manila Bay sunset
items.summary: Famous sunsets over the bay from the long seafront promenade.

items.name: Taal Volcano and Tagaytay
items.summary: A volcano inside a lake, seen from the cool Tagaytay ridge.
items.expect: About 2 hours by car; volcano access depends on activity.
items.tip: Have bulalo soup on the ridge.
items.why: A volcano in a lake in a volcano.

items.name: Adobo
items.summary: Chicken or pork stewed in vinegar, soy, garlic and bay leaf.

items.name: Binondo food crawl
items.summary: Dumplings, hopia and fried siopao along Ongpin Street.

items.name: Halo-halo
items.summary: Shaved ice with beans, jellies, fruit, ube and leche flan.

cashTip: Carry pesos in small notes for jeepneys, tricycles and small shops; ATMs can run dry on islands, so bring enough cash.
name: El Nido · Palawan
summary: El Nido, on the island of Palawan, looks out on Bacuit Bay's limestone islands, white beaches and turquoise lagoons. Boat tours visit the Big and Small Lagoons, secret beaches and snorkel reefs.
seasonNote: December to May is dry, with calm seas; island tours can be cancelled in rough weather from June to November.
arrival: Fly direct to El Nido from Manila on small planes, or to Puerto Princesa and take a 5 to 6 hour van. Ferries run from Coron.
gettingAround: Tricycles around town; island-hopping boats leave from El Nido beach.
foodTip: Grilled seafood, kinilaw (Filipino ceviche) and mango shakes.
buyTip: Pearls, woven bags and local cashews.

items.name: Big and Small Lagoons
items.summary: Turquoise lagoons inside limestone cliffs, explored by kayak.
items.expect: On island-hopping Tour A; an environmental fee applies.

items.name: Bacuit Bay island hopping
items.summary: Islands, secret beaches and snorkel reefs.
items.tip: Choose a small-group or private boat.
items.why: Some of the world's best seascapes.

items.name: Taraw Cliff
items.summary: A sharp limestone climb above town with a sweeping view.
items.expect: Guided only; steep and sharp rock.
items.tip: Go with a guide at sunrise.

items.name: Las Cabanas Beach
items.summary: A sunset beach with a zipline to an island.

items.name: Nacpan Beach
items.summary: A 4 km curve of golden sand backed by palms.
items.expect: About 40 minutes by tricycle or scooter.
items.tip: Climb the hill for the twin-beach view.

items.name: Coron
items.summary: Shipwreck diving and Kayangan Lake.

items.name: Puerto Princesa Underground River
items.wiki: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park
items.summary: A navigable underground river through a cave.
items.expect: A permit is needed; book ahead.
items.tip: Combine with your arrival in Puerto Princesa.

items.name: Grilled seafood
items.summary: Fresh fish, squid and prawns grilled on the beach.
items.expect: Choose your catch at the counter.

items.name: Kinilaw
items.summary: Raw fish cured in vinegar with ginger, onion and chilli.
items.tip: Try it on the boat lunch.

items.name: Mango shake
items.summary: Thick shakes made with sweet Philippine mangoes.
items.tip: Have one after a boat day.

cashTip: Carry pesos in small notes for jeepneys, tricycles and small shops; ATMs can run dry on islands, so bring enough cash.
name: Cebu
tagline: Where Christianity came to the Philippines
summary: Cebu is the Philippines' oldest city, where Magellan landed in 1521. Its churches and forts tell that story, the Sinulog festival fills the streets in January, and the island has some of the country's best diving, waterfalls and beaches.
seasonNote: December to May is dry. The Sinulog festival is the third Sunday of January. June to November brings rain and typhoons.
arrival: Mactan-Cebu International Airport is 30 to 60 minutes from the city, with flights from Manila, Singapore, Seoul and Tokyo.
gettingAround: Grab and taxis in the city; buses or a driver to the south of the island.
foodTip: Cebu lechon (roast pig), puso hanging rice and fresh seafood.
buyTip: Dried mangoes, guitars from Mactan and shell crafts.

connections.note: Via Puerto Princesa or direct seasonal flights.

items.name: Magellan's Cross
items.summary: A wooden cross in a painted pavilion, planted by Magellan's expedition in 1521.
items.why: The start of Christianity in the Philippines.

items.name: Basilica del Santo Niño
items.summary: The oldest Catholic church in the country, home of the Santo Niño statue.
items.tip: Visit on a Friday to see the devotions.

items.name: Fort San Pedro
items.summary: The oldest Spanish triangular fort in the Philippines.

items.name: Temple of Leah
items.summary: A Roman-style temple built as a monument to love, with city views.
items.tip: Go late afternoon for city views.

items.name: Cebu Taoist Temple
items.summary: A colourful Taoist temple on a hill, built by the Chinese community.

items.name: Mactan beaches
items.summary: Resort beaches and island-hopping boats near the airport.
items.tip: Take an island-hopping tour to Nalusuan.
items.why: Easy beach time near the city.

items.name: Kawasan Falls
items.summary: Turquoise cascades in the jungle, the end of canyoneering trips.
items.expect: About 3 hours by car; canyoneering needs a guide.

items.name: Moalboal sardine run
items.summary: Millions of sardines swirl just off the shore; turtles too.
items.expect: About 3 hours by car; snorkel from the beach.

items.name: Cebu lechon
items.summary: Whole roast pig with crackling skin, stuffed with herbs.
items.why: Said to be the best in the Philippines.

items.name: Puso hanging rice
items.summary: Rice cooked in woven coconut leaf pouches.

items.name: Sutukil seafood
items.summary: Choose fresh seafood and have it grilled, stewed or raw.
